convert: Decodes your file and re-encodes it in the format you choose using the FFmpeg.wasm engine that runs on your device. Lossy formats expose a bitrate control
compress: Re-encodes audio at a lower bitrate, optionally mono, to cut file size while keeping the content. It reports the exact before and after size and the byte
to-wav: Decode any supported audio file and export a universally compatible, uncompressed PCM WAV. WAV plays everywhere and is the safest format for editing.
to-mp3: Encodes to MP3 with the LAME encoder at 96-320 kbps. MP3 plays on virtually every device, so it is the safe choice for sharing and playback.
to-flac: FLAC stores every sample of the original with lossless compression, so it is typically 40-60% smaller than WAV while remaining a perfect copy of the source
to-m4a: AAC generally sounds better than MP3 at the same bitrate, and M4A is natively supported by iOS, macOS, Android and modern browsers.
to-ogg: Ogg Vorbis and Opus are royalty-free formats widely used on the web, in games and in open-source software. Opus gives excellent quality at low bitrates.
to-aiff: Convert audio to uncompressed AIFF, the classic Apple lossless format. Ideal for macOS tools, Logic Pro and hardware samplers that expect native AIFF.
audio-to-base64: Reads the file and produces a Base64 string plus a ready-to-paste data URI. Base64 grows the payload by about 33%. Use it for small assets embedded in CSS
base64-to-audio: Decode a Base64 string or a full data URI back into a playable, downloadable audio file. Bench reconstructs the original bytes and detects the format.
ringtone-maker: Crop any song to a phone-ready ringtone clip of up to 30 seconds, add a smooth fade in and out, and export it as MP3 or M4A for your device.
batch-rename: Rename and export several audio files at once with a shared prefix, sequence numbers and an output format, then download them or a single ZIP.
audio-zip: Bundle several audio files into a single standard ZIP archive for one-click download. Each file is validated as it is read and the total size is reported.
trimmer: Decodes the file, draws its waveform and lets you drag precise start and end points. Export the selected range losslessly to WAV or re-encode to MP3.
silence-remover: Scans for silence below a threshold you set and either strips it out or reports it as a map. Useful for tightening voice recordings and podcasts.
joiner: Combines files end to end, resampling and re-encoding to a single consistent output. Add a crossfade to blend tracks smoothly.
splitter: Cuts a single file into multiple pieces either at times you set or into equally sized chunks, then offers them as individual files or a ZIP.
fade: Add a smooth fade-in, a fade-out or both so a track never starts or stops abruptly. Fade lengths are independent and clamped to the file length.
reverse: Play an audio file backwards for sound design, hidden-message checks and creative edits. Reversing is exact and can be exported losslessly as WAV.
speed: Speed up or slow down audio from 0.5x to 3x while keeping the pitch steady, using pitch-preserving time-stretch so speech stays clear and intelligible.
pitch: Shifts pitch by resampling and compensating with time-stretch so the duration stays similar. The result is an estimate and can introduce artefacts at large
volume-adjust: Either applies a gain offset you set or normalises the whole file to a target peak level. A safety limiter prevents clipping when you boost.
loop-maker: Repeat a chosen section of audio a set number of times to build a seamless loop, with an optional crossfade between repeats to avoid clicks at the joins.
crossfade: Blend two tracks together with a real equal-power crossfade at a duration you choose. Both files must be long enough to overlap for the selected length.
channel-tools: Reshape stereo audio: swap left and right, keep one channel only, downmix to mono or duplicate one channel to both sides. Fixes reversed recordings.
noise-reducer: Reduce steady background noise such as hiss, hum and air conditioning with a genuine FFT spectral denoiser and an adjustable noise floor.
voice-enhancer: Applies a speech-tuned chain: high-pass to remove rumble, a presence boost, gentle dynamic compression and a limiter. It improves intelligibility on dry
equalizer: Boost or cut bass, treble and a selectable mid band with real biquad peaking and shelf filters. A limiter protects the output from clipping after boosts.
loudness-normalizer: Measures integrated loudness with the ITU-R BS.1770/EBU R128 loudnorm filter and normalises to your target, with a true-peak ceiling so it never clips.
clipping-detector: Scan a file for clipped samples and report how often, where and how loudly it distorts, so you can catch problems before release or diagnose a recording.
silence-detector: Map every silent gap in a file with its start time, end time and duration. Set a threshold and minimum gap length, then read the full table of gaps.
recorder: Requests microphone access only when you click record, shows a live level meter and a timer, and lets you trim and export the take. Nothing is uploaded.
mic-check: Lists your audio input devices, shows a real-time input level meter and a peak-hold readout so you can confirm the microphone and gain before recording.
stereo-test: Play a generated tone through the left, right or both channels, or alternate between them, to confirm your speakers and headphones are wired correctly.
tone-generator: Generate a precise sine tone or a musical note at any frequency from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, preview it and download it as a WAV for testing speakers or hearing.
noise-generator: Generate white, pink or brown noise with the correct spectral shape, play it to preview and download it as a WAV for masking, sleep, focus or room testing.
metronome: Play an accurate click track at any tempo from 30 to 300 BPM with a configurable time signature and a louder accent on the downbeat for practice sessions.
bpm-detector: Estimates tempo from onset energy and suggests a key from chroma-like spectral energy. Both are estimates and can be wrong on complex or non-percussive
spectrogram: Render a spectrogram of any audio file so you can see its frequencies over time, using a Web Audio FFT and a downloadable PNG image as the result.
waveform-image: Generate a clean waveform PNG from any audio file for podcast art, video overlays or the web. Choose the size, colours, background and bar or wave style.
metadata-viewer: Reads embedded tags and the audio properties your browser can decode, and shows them clearly. It also reads raw ID3v1/ID3v2 tags directly from the bytes
id3-editor: Copies the audio stream and writes updated metadata using FFmpeg, so the audio content is preserved. The output is a new file; the original is never
loudness-analyzer: Runs real loudness measurement (EBU R128 via FFmpeg loudnorm/ebur128) and basic RMS/peak analysis, then reports whether the file meets a chosen platform
integrity-check: Checks the file signature against its extension, attempts a full decode and reports truncated or corrupt files instead of silently failing.
duplicate-finder: Computes a hash of the decoded audio (not just the bytes) so the same audio saved in two containers is detected. Similar-sounding but different files are
mime-checker: Reads the leading bytes to identify the true format, flags a mismatched extension and shows the MIME type a server would send.
player-generator: Produces ready-to-paste HTML for an audio player with a proper <source>, controls and fallback text. Values are HTML-escaped.
rss-validator: Check a podcast RSS feed for missing or invalid enclosure tags: an audio URL, a length value and a valid audio MIME type, with a clear issue report.
